skill.name: frontend-dev-guidelines
skill.description: Provides practical frontend guidance for React, Next.js, TypeScript, routing, data fetching, forms, styling, loading states, and performance.
skill.summary: Build consistent, type-safe React frontends with documented architecture and implementation patterns.

security_audit.summary: All 151 static findings are false positives in instructional Markdown and TypeScript examples. Dynamic imports use fixed paths, backticks are documentation syntax, and relative imports do not access the filesystem. Network examples use application clients or a same-origin endpoint, and no prompt injection or malicious intent was found.

content.user_title: Build Modern React and Next.js Frontends
content.value_statement: Modern frontend projects need consistent architecture, data fetching, state, styling, and loading patterns. This skill provides practical React, Next.js, TypeScript, MUI, shadcn/ui, Supabase, and TanStack Query guidance.
actual_capabilities: Structures pages, routes, feature folders, imports, and public exports for maintainable frontend projects.
Guides Server Component, Client Component, Server Action, and lazy-loading decisions.
Builds typed forms with React Hook Form and Zod validation patterns.
Explains Supabase access, API service layers, TanStack Query caching, mutations, and invalidation.
Adds Suspense boundaries, loading interfaces, error handling, and user notifications.
Improves rendering performance through memoization, cleanup, code splitting, and focused subscriptions.
limitations: The skill provides instructions and examples but does not install dependencies or verify runtime behavior.
The main guide favors Next.js and shadcn/ui, while several resources use TanStack Router and MUI.
Examples require adaptation for project authentication, authorization, testing, and API contracts.
Framework APIs can change, so version-specific details should be checked against current documentation.

use_cases.title: Create a New Product Page
use_cases.description: Plan a typed page with data loading, validation, responsive UI, and clear error states.

use_cases.title: Standardize a React Codebase
use_cases.description: Define consistent feature folders, imports, components, query keys, and styling conventions.

use_cases.title: Review Frontend Performance
use_cases.description: Identify unnecessary client code, broad subscriptions, missing cleanup, and useful lazy-loading boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Typed Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React component for [feature]. Use TypeScript, accessible controls, responsive styling, and explicit loading and empty states.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Validated Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a [form name] form with React Hook Form and Zod. Include validation messages, submission feedback, and typed values.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Data Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement data loading and mutations for [entity]. Use the project API client, stable query keys, cache invalidation, and recoverable errors.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Frontend Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [feature paths] for component boundaries, routing, type safety, accessibility, loading behavior, caching, and performance. Apply focused fixes and explain tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Create an account settings page with profile editing and server data.
output: A server-rendered page loads the initial account record.
A client form handles typed validation and submission feedback.
A mutation refreshes account data after a successful update.

output_examples.input: Review a slow dashboard with several large panels.
output: Heavy panels receive focused lazy-loading boundaries.
Repeated calculations and callbacks are memoized only where measurable.
Network effects include cancellation and cleanup behavior.

output_examples.input: Organize a new billing feature in an existing React project.
output: The feature receives clear component, hook, API, helper, and type boundaries.
Public exports keep imports stable across the application.
Project aliases and naming conventions remain consistent.

best_practices: Match recommendations to the project framework, versions, component library, and existing conventions.
Keep server data, local UI state, and form state in their appropriate ownership layers.
Request tests and verification for user-facing behavior, data mutations, and error recovery.
anti_patterns: Do not add client rendering to components that have no interactive requirement.
Do not copy examples without adapting authentication, authorization, routes, and API contracts.
Do not add memoization, global state, or lazy loading without a clear performance or ownership need.

faq.question: Which projects fit this skill?
faq.answer: It best fits TypeScript React projects, especially Next.js applications using modern routing, forms, and data tools.

faq.question: Does the skill edit project files?
faq.answer: The connected AI tool can edit files when requested. The skill supplies implementation guidance and examples.

faq.question: Is shadcn/ui required?
faq.answer: No. The main guide prefers shadcn/ui, while resource examples also cover MUI and adaptable component patterns.

faq.question: Does it support Server Components?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Server Components, Client Components, Server Actions, direct data loading, and interactive boundaries.

faq.question: Which data tools are covered?
faq.answer: The guidance covers Supabase, configured API clients, TanStack Query, Suspense queries, mutations, and cache invalidation.

faq.question: Does it provide complete testing coverage?
faq.answer: No. Testing is mentioned, but examples do not provide complete unit, integration, end-to-end, or accessibility test suites.
